title: Kimi K3 core membership
catchSummary: Credits are shared across one pool with 5-hour and weekly controls — heavy sprint days can throttle before the month ends.

verdict: Pick Kimi K3 membership if you run steady agentic coding volume and want one predictable bill. At Allegretto ($39/mo, about $31/mo effective annually) it beats pay-as-you-go once you clear roughly 40–50 heavy tasks a month — below that, PAYG or a free route costs less. The constraint: a single shared credit pool plus 5-hour and weekly controls means marathon sessions can stall mid-sprint.
catches: One shared credit pool: membership usage draws from a single balance, so parallel projects and long agent runs drain it together
5-hour and weekly controls: burst caps can throttle you mid-day even when the monthly balance looks healthy
Tier jump is steep: Allegretto ($39) to Allegro ($99) is a 2.5x step — usage between those tiers is priced comparatively poorly
Annual discount is upfront cash: the ~20% effective saving requires a full-year prepay with terms you must confirm first
limits: k3-256k context with high thinking-on: long sessions consume materially more than short completions
Coding endpoint (https://api.kimi.com/coding/) vs PAYG key billing are different routes — pick the wrong one and the membership may not apply
Weekly controls reset on the provider's schedule, not yours — confirm the reset window before planning sprints
Fair-use style gating can apply to extreme patterns; the weekly controls are the mechanism to watch
access_route: Subscribe to Kimi K3 membership on the official site, then point coding tools at the coding endpoint (https://api.kimi.com/coding/) — not a PAYG API key — so usage draws from the membership pool.

claim_steps.step: Open the official membership pricing page and compare the tiers against PAYG pricing.
Pick the tier that covers a normal week plus headroom — Moderato $19 for light use, Allegretto $39 for steady coding, Allegro $99 or Vivace $199 for heavy agent fleets.
Check renewal terms (monthly vs annual effective $15 / $31 / $79 / $159) and the cancellation path before entering payment details.
After subscribing, configure tools to use https://api.kimi.com/coding/ and verify the first session draws from membership, not PAYG billing.

economics: Think in effective cost per task: monthly price divided by tasks you actually complete. Allegretto at $39 over 120 tasks is about $0.33 per task — less than half the $0.80 illustrative PAYG reference for a 100k-token task.
The break-even against the $0.80/task reference is about 49 tasks a month on Allegretto ($39 ÷ $0.80) and about 24 tasks on Moderato ($19 ÷ $0.80). Below those lines, PAYG or a free tier is cheaper.
Annual billing drops Allegretto to about $31/mo effective (~$372 upfront), which moves break-even down to roughly 39 tasks a month — worth it only if your volume is stable year-round.
The shared pool has a throughput cost too: if 5-hour or weekly controls idle you for half a day each week, discount the membership's value by that lost throughput before comparing.

faq.q: What does Kimi K3 membership cost as of the Sep 2026 snapshot?
faq.a: Moderato $19, Allegretto $39, Allegro $99, and Vivace $199 per month. Annual billing lowers the effective monthly cost to about $15 / $31 / $79 / $159, paid upfront. Prices verified in the Sep 6 2026 snapshot — re-check the official page before paying.

faq.q: How does the shared credit pool restrict usage?
faq.a: Membership usage draws from one shared credit pool, and 5-hour plus weekly controls can throttle burst usage even when monthly balance remains. Spread heavy agent runs across the week instead of one marathon day.

faq.q: Coding endpoint or PAYG — which do I use?
faq.a: Use the coding endpoint at https://api.kimi.com/coding/ for membership billing. A PAYG API key bills separately, so pointing tools at the wrong route means the membership does not cover that usage.

faq.q: When is annual billing worth it?
faq.a: When your monthly volume is stable and clears break-even (about 39 tasks/mo on Allegretto annual vs ~49 on monthly, against the $0.80/task reference). If your usage is seasonal, stay monthly until the pattern is proven.

faq.q: Is API credit use cheaper than a $20 subscription, and at what usage?
faq.a: At the $0.80/task reference, $19 of pay-as-you-go buys about 24 tasks — below that, credits or a free route are cheaper; above it, the $19 Moderato month is cheaper. The routes do not mix: a PAYG key bills separately from the coding-endpoint membership, so check which one your tools actually hit.
This is a research snapshot from Sep 6 2026, not a live checkout feed. Prices, pools, and controls can change.
